info.title: EduMatcher API Gateway
info.description:
REST/JSON and WebSocket gateway for EduMatcher order entry and market data.

## Authentication

Every request carries an API key as a bearer token:

    Authorization: Bearer <api_key>

Keys are configured per gateway process under `api_gateways.<name>.credentials`
in the engine config. A key maps to one of two things:

* a **trading gateway** (`gateway_id` set) -- may submit, amend and cancel
  orders and read its own orders, fills and positions. What it may do beyond
  that depends on the engine **role** of that gateway: `TRADER`,
  `MARKET_MAKER` (adds quoting) or `ADMIN` (adds the `/admin` endpoints);
* a **read-only key** (`gateway_id` null) -- may read public data only:
  `/reference/*`, `/news`, `/companies/{symbol}`, `/history/trades`,
  `/history/daily` and the other public history endpoints, `/bootstrap/trader`.
  Everything gateway-scoped answers `403 READ_ONLY`.

## Asynchronous order entry

`POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on orders are **asynchronous**: the gateway hands
the request to the matching engine and, by default, answers `202` with
`status: PENDING` straight away. The engine's verdict (accepted, rejected,
filled) arrives on the private WebSocket stream. Add `?wait=ack` to hold the
response until the engine acknowledges, up to the gateway's `wait_ack_sec`
timeout; the verdict is then in `accepted`, `reject_code` and `event`.

## Errors

Every error uses one envelope, whatever the cause:

    {"error": {"code": "VALIDATION", "message": "...", "field": "price",
               "reject_code": "TICK_VIOLATION"}}

That includes an unknown path (`404 NOT_FOUND`), a wrong method
(`405 METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`) and a gateway bug (`500 INTERNAL_ERROR`). `code` is
the HTTP-level category; `reject_code` is the same vocabulary the engine uses
on `order.ack` rejects, so REST and ALF clients see identical values for the
same mistake. `client_tag` / `request_tag` are echoed back when the request
carried one. Validation failures are always `400`.

## Status codes

`200` means the response carries the outcome; `202` means the request was
handed on and the outcome follows on a WebSocket. An order submit, cancel or
amend is `202` by default and `200` with `?wait=ack`. An admin command the
engine refuses is `409` with a command-specific code.

## Rate limiting

Write endpoints (POST/PATCH/DELETE) are limited per API key by a token bucket
(`rate_limit.writes_per_second`, `rate_limit.burst`). Over the limit the answer
is `429 RATE_LIMITED`. Reads are not limited.

## Prices and time

Prices are decimal display prices (`187.25`), always on the symbol's tick grid
(`tick_decimals` in `/reference/symbols`); an off-grid price is `400 TICK_VIOLATION`.
Timestamps named `ts_ns` / `*_ns` are epoch nanoseconds; `ts` in history rows is
ISO-8601 UTC. `date` filters are trading days in the exchange's own timezone
(`session_timezone` in `GET /session`).

## WebSocket

Live streams are WebSockets under `/api/v1/ws/` and are not part of this
OpenAPI document: `/api/v1/ws/private` (orders, fills, quotes),
`/api/v1/ws/market-data` (book, trades, depth, auction, session, halts, news),
and, for ADMIN keys, `/api/v1/ws/admin/monitor` and `/api/v1/ws/admin/sim`.

post.description: Send a new order to the matching engine under the caller's gateway. Which fields are required depends on `order_type`: LIMIT/FOK/IOC need `price`; MARKET forbids price; STOP needs `stop_price`; STOP_LIMIT needs both; ICEBERG needs `price` and a smaller `visible_qty`; TRAILING_STOP needs `trail_offset` and may set an initial `stop_price`. Any other of these fields is rejected. Prices must lie on the symbol's tick grid. `client_tag` is an opaque label echoed on every event for this order. Returns `202` (`PENDING`); with `?wait=ack`, `200` and the engine's verdict in the same response, or `202` with `ack_timeout: true` if the verdict did not come in time. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make a retry safe.

post.description: Cancel an order and submit a new one in a single call. The body is a full order, exactly as for `POST /orders`, on the same symbol. The replacement is only sent once the engine has confirmed the cancel; a refused cancel (the order already filled, say) is `409 REPLACE_REJECTED` and nothing is sent. The replacement is a new order (new id, new time priority); `?wait=ack` waits for its verdict too. Send an `Idempotency-Key` to make a retry safe.

OrderDisplay.title: OrderDisplay
OrderDisplay.description:
One resting order as the engine reports it in an `order.orders` snapshot, in
display units. It is `Order.to_dict()` with price, stop_price and trail_offset
converted from ticks to display money - the projection `order_to_display_dict`
builds so an operator reads prices in the same money the book shows, not raw
ticks. `timestamp` is carried through as `ts_ns` unconverted (AR-0.3b): unlike
price, a raw nanosecond integer is exactly what a post-mortem needs to compare
against `trade.executed.ts_ns` and the rest of the wire's ordering convention,
and converting it to seconds here would only have to be undone by anything
that wanted to compare it. `spec/messages/index.yaml`'s family made the same
call for the same reason in AR-0.3; this type was out of scope for that pass
(it is not part of the index family) and CP-0's own checklist item 3 is what
caught it being left behind. Gateway_id is not included here; it is topic-only
(part of the message topic as order.orders.{gateway_id}, not part of the
record). The record contains the order state (id, symbol, side, etc.) exactly
as Order.to_dict() produces, minus gateway_id; the eleven nullable ones ride
as null when unset.

SmpAction.title: SmpAction
SmpAction.description:
Self Match Prevention action — applied when an incoming order would trade
against a resting order from the same gateway.

NONE             — explicitly disabled; self-trades are allowed
CANCEL_AGGRESSOR — cancel the incoming order, resting order stays
CANCEL_RESTING   — cancel the resting order, continue matching
CANCEL_BOTH      — cancel both orders

``Order.smp_action`` (and ``ComboLeg.smp_action``) is typed
``SmpAction | None`` rather than defaulting to ``NONE`` outright: ``None``
means the client did not specify ``SMP=`` at all, which is distinct from
an *explicit* ``SMP=NONE`` (a deliberate request to allow self-trades).
Client-facing processes (``alf_gwy``, ``alf_console``, ``api_gateway``)
preserve that distinction when parsing the wire request; the engine
resolves ``None`` to the order's gateway-configured default
(``participants[].smp_action``, falling back to ``NONE`` itself if the
gateway has none configured) before the order reaches the matching
engine — see ``Engine._resolve_smp_action`` in ``engine/main.py``. Code
that inspects ``Order.smp_action`` after that resolution point (e.g. the
order book) can safely assume it is a concrete member, never ``None``.

gateways asking at the same moment get different values for the same
instrument, which is why they travel on this reply rather than in the
reference bundle.

WeeklySchedule.title: WeeklySchedule
WeeklySchedule.description:
A fully-resolved weekly session schedule: one `SessionTimes` per weekday
(mon..sun, any of which may be null for CLOSED) plus a separate holidays
entry, mirroring `edumatcher.engine.config_loader.ScheduleConfig`. The
`weekdays`/ `weekend` shortcuts and per-day overrides in the YAML are already
resolved by the time this is built -- every field here is one concrete day,
never a shortcut. `today`/`today_is_holiday` are a server-computed
convenience: the engine already runs the same `python-holidays` lookup for pm-
scheduler, so it resolves "which entry applies right now" once and publishes
the answer, rather than making every client (in particular a browser) carry
its own holiday calendar just to answer that one question. `today` is still
`SessionTimes | null` -- null means CLOSED today, exactly like any other day
slot. `upcoming_holidays` answers the next question, "when is the exchange
next on its holiday schedule", the same way. It is computed when the record is
built and covers a year, so a client picks the first entry on or after its own
today rather than trusting the list to start there.

tags.name: orders
tags.description: Order entry and management for the caller's own gateway: submit, amend, cancel, replace, OCO, combos, market-maker quotes and mass cancel. Requires a trading key. Writes are asynchronous -- see *Asynchronous order entry* above.

tags.name: reference
tags.description: Static venue configuration (symbols, tick sizes, collars, circuit-breaker ladders, indexes, trading schedule) and live session/halt state, plus news and company profiles. Reference endpoints are open to read-only keys; every response that derives from the reference bundle carries `config_version`, a hash that changes whenever the configuration does.

tags.name: history
tags.description: Read-only history from the pm-stats database: the caller's own order events and fills, public trades, daily OHLC, intraday snapshots and index series. List endpoints are keyset-paginated: pass the response's `next_cursor` back as `after` to get the next page; `has_more` says whether another page may exist. `retained_from` on order-event endpoints is the point pm-stats prunes at (null when nothing is pruned).

tags.name: bootstrap
tags.description: One-request startup payloads (reference data, session, positions, open orders, today's fills, halts, capability flags) so a client can render after a single call. Optional sections that time out come back `null` and are named in `incomplete`; required sections turn the whole call into `503 ENGINE_TIMEOUT`.

tags.name: admin
tags.description: Operator endpoints. Require a key whose gateway has the engine role `ADMIN`; any other trading key gets `403 ROLE_DENIED`. Covers session control, reference reload, circuit-breaker halt/resume, kill switches, index rebalancing, and cross-gateway views of orders, positions and gateways.
